answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation that vests over time. An agent posts a bond, say a jade deposit locked in escrow, and earns trust only by completing verified work across many epochs, like climbing from a knoll to a summit. New identities start near zero weight, so spinning up a thousand sybils costs a thousand bonds plus months of honest history, while a single real agent's reputation compounds. Attackers can buy in, but they cannot buy time.
